required_facts_checked: The goal was a compact Python search library that was local, easy to integrate and persistent.
minsearch supported text and vector search with a simple API but kept its index in memory and lost data after process restart.
The library was needed for an AI Engineering Buildcamp project with ingestion independent of the RAG agent.
Requirements included Python, easy local setup without Docker, and regular text plus vector search.
Elasticsearch was considered too large and costly for the small-scale use case, while Qdrant and PostgreSQL would require an external service or Docker.
ChatGPT suggested SQLite text search, but SQLite lacked vector search by default.
lshashing kept hash tables in memory, SparseLSH lacked SQLite support and narrow-down used a native Rust extension.
Locality-sensitive hashing was chosen because random projections were already understood and could be debugged directly.
The project began as LightSearch and was renamed SQLiteSearch because litesearch was already taken on PyPI.
ChatGPT produced the design plan, Claude Code implemented it from plan.md and tests were requested.
SQLiteSearch stores its index, tables and metadata in one SQLite file without a separate server process.
The release workflow uses Claude Code /release and /init-library commands for package publication and project setup.
unsupported_claims_removed: Removed claims about production-scale performance, benchmark results or universal suitability not stated in the source.
Removed claims that implied the AI tools independently made the design decisions.
substantive_edits: Rewrote the draft as a first-person account moving from requirements through research, implementation and architecture.
Preserved the small-project scope and the reasons for rejecting existing options.
Clarified the handoff from ChatGPT's research and plan to Claude Code's implementation.
